title: When is a task done?

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: The task being closed, as the asker named it.

computation:
# line 1 — the proof, must fail when the feature is broken
node scripts/okf.mjs --check

# line 2 — no regression
bash scripts/check-skills.sh

# line 3 — written in the PR body, not a command
# not run: <what and why>

answer_spec.sub: The first line must fail when the feature is broken. An auditor re-runs the commands; an agent never verifies its own work.

title: How do I end the day?
question_patterns: how do i end the day
what do i queue for tonight
computation:
# 1. the state file, rewritten every session
cat > STATE.md <<'EOF'
## Where we are
## Last 3 decisions
## Open work
## Do not do
EOF

# 2. queue 1-3 contractor cards, each with its own done-gate command,
#    then let the overnight agent work them on an integration branch

# 3. stop. the morning reviews the diffs.

answer_spec.sub: One paragraph per task, its own context, a one-line finish line, a done-gate. Nothing merges without a human reading the diff.

title: How do I start the day?
question_patterns: how do i start the day
what should i work on first
computation:
# the delta, not the corpus
git log --oneline --since=yesterday
gh pr list
gh pr checks

# the state probe: branch, last 3 decisions, top open task
cat STATE.md

answer_spec.sub: Load state, not history. A rejected plan is the cheapest failure: the agent proposes the day in 5 lines, the human trims.

title: How do I cut a release?
question_patterns: how do i cut a release

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version to release, as the asker wrote it (e.g. 1.2.0).

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: What is released: an app, a package, or the version itself. Copy the asker's words.

computation:
# 1. the done gate, local
npm ci
npm run check

# 2. the version tag
git tag v:version
git push origin v:version

# 3. the Release workflow publishes; verify its run is green
gh run list --workflow=release.yml --limit 1

answer_spec.sub: Checks first, then the tag. The Release workflow does the publishing; the release is done when its run is green.
